protocol.instrument_name: Authority – Supply of specified restricted substances by pharmacists – management of mild, acute musculoskeletal pain
protocol.instrument_version: Dated: 25 February 2026 (signed by Dr Kerry Chant, Chief Health Officer, Delegation Number PH380, PH381, PH427; revokes the instrument of the same purpose dated 30 January 2025)
protocol.effective_date: Commences on publication (no calendar date printed); cancelled on 1 March 2027 unless earlier cancelled
protocol.legal_basis: Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Act 1966, section 10(4)(d); Poisons and Therapeutic Goods Regulation 2008, clauses 170 and 171 for the purpose of clause 53
protocol.supervision_model: approved pharmacist (document's own term) — a pharmacist holding general registration under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law (NSW) who is employed or engaged in an 'approved pharmacy', has successfully completed the specified training options, and has provided NSW Health with their full name, contact details, pharmacist registration number, intended services and location of services via the expanded services application form
protocol.scope_summary: NSW Health Authority authorising an approved pharmacist to supply the oral restricted substances listed in clause 2 (celecoxib, etoricoxib, indometacin, ketoprofen, meloxicam, naproxen IR, naproxen MR, piroxicam, diclofenac) to an applicable patient aged 18 years or over for the management of mild, acute musculoskeletal pain otherwise than on prescription, subject to in-person consultation, clinical record-keeping (7 years), consent-to-share and quantity conditions (absolute cap: supply not longer than 12 weeks). Clinical assessment limits, age/other-factor supply limits and referral circumstances are set by the external NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Mild, Acute Musculoskeletal Pain, which is not printed in this instrument.

inclusion.text: The patient is an 'applicable patient', meaning a patient 18 years of age or over.
The pharmacist must only supply a medicine indicated in clause 2 for the management of mild, acute musculoskeletal pain.

The medicine is one of the oral forms listed in clause 2: celecoxib, etoricoxib, indometacin, ketoprofen, meloxicam, naproxen immediate-release, naproxen modified-release (clause 2 list begins on page 1) plus piroxicam and diclofenac (printed on page 2).

provenance.section_heading: 2) Restricted substance to which this instrument applies

inclusion.text: The pharmacist must not supply a medicine indicated in clause 2 in a quantity that exceeds the duration of management specified in the Practice Standard, except where the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack exceeds the quantity specified in the Practice Standard (in which case the smallest available size may be supplied).
Despite clause 3(c), the pharmacist must not supply a medicine indicated in clause 2 in a quantity which would result in supply for a period that is longer than 12 weeks.

The pharmacist acts in accordance with the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Mild, Acute Musculoskeletal Pain approved by the Chief Health Officer and published on the NSW Health website for the purpose of this Authority, including in relation to any limitations on the supply of medicines indicated in clause 2 to a patient based on their age or other factor, and circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional.
The patient and pharmacist must both be physically present at the approved pharmacy premises, for consultation with the patient to occur prior to supply.

The supplier is an 'approved pharmacist' as defined: holds general registration under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law (NSW); is employed or engaged in an 'approved pharmacy'; has successfully completed the specified training options; and has provided NSW Health with their full name, contact details, pharmacist registration number, intended services and location of services via the prescribed form.

exclusion.text: The patient is under 18 years of age (an 'applicable patient' means a patient 18 years of age or over).
The medicine would be supplied for anything other than the management of mild, acute musculoskeletal pain.
The medicine is not one of the oral forms listed in clause 2 of this instrument.

provenance.section_heading: 2) Restricted substance to which this instrument applies

exclusion.text: The quantity supplied would result in supply for a period that is longer than 12 weeks (absolute cap under clause 3(d)).

The quantity exceeds the duration of management specified in the Practice Standard and the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack does not exceed that quantity (clauses 3(b) and 3(c)). The duration of management figure itself is not printed in this instrument.
The consultation does not take place with the patient and the pharmacist both physically present at the approved pharmacy premises prior to supply.

The pharmacist is not an 'approved pharmacist', the pharmacy is not an 'approved pharmacy' (including consulting room requirements), or the pharmacist has not provided their details to NSW Health via the prescribed form.

A limitation on supply based on the patient's age or other factor applies under the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Mild, Acute Musculoskeletal Pain, or the referral circumstances in that Practice Standard apply (clause 3(e)). The specific limits/circumstances are not printed in this instrument.

exclusion_exceptions.text: If the smallest available size of the manufacturer's pack of the medicine exceeds the quantity specified in the Practice Standard, the pharmacist may supply the medicine in the smallest available size (exception to the quantity limit in clause 3(b); does not override the 12-week cap in clause 3(d)).

treatments.notes: Listed in clause 2 as an oral form to which the instrument applies. Dose, strength, frequency and duration of management are not printed in this instrument; quantity is limited by the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Mild, Acute Musculoskeletal Pain (clause 3(b)) and in any event must not result in supply longer than 12 weeks (clause 3(d)).

red_flags.trigger_text: The pharmacist must act in accordance with the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Mild, Acute Musculoskeletal Pain ... including ... circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional.
Despite clause 3(c), the pharmacist must not supply a medicine indicated in clause 2 of this instrument in a quantity which would result in supply for a period that is longer than 12 weeks.
An 'applicable patient' means a patient 18 years of age or over.
The patient and pharmacist must both be physically present at the approved pharmacy premises, for consultation with the patient to occur prior to supply.

routine: Circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional as set out in the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Mild, Acute Musculoskeletal Pain approved by the Chief Health Officer and published on the NSW Health website (clause 3(e)).

review_followup.when: Within a week following the consultation, if the patient consents to the disclosure
review_followup.what: Share the record of the consultation (and any subsequent consultations, including adverse events) with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice, where the patient has one; communication should ensure patient confidentiality is maintained and use of a secure digital messaging platform is considered best practice.

conditions: The pharmacist must seek the patient's consent to share a record of the consultation and any subsequent consultations (including adverse events) with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice, where the patient has one; if the patient consents, the record must be shared within a week following the consultation (clause 3(j)).

references: NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Mild, Acute Musculoskeletal Pain approved by the Chief Health Officer and published on the NSW Health website for the purpose of this Authority (clause 3(e), page 2).

NSW Health expanded services application form: https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/pharmaceutical/Pages/expanded-services-application.aspx (clause 3(f), page 2; definition of 'approved pharmacist', pages 3-4).

open_questions.topic: Clinical assessment limits and referral circumstances are external to this instrument
open_questions.observed: Clause 3(b) refers to 'the duration of management specified in the Practice Standard' and clause 3(e) refers to 'any limitations on the supply ... based on their age or other factor, and circumstances where a patient must be referred to a medical practitioner or other healthcare professional', but the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Mild, Acute Musculoskeletal Pain is not reproduced in this document. No assessment steps, no numeric duration of management, no age limits other than 18+, and no specific referral triggers are printed.
open_questions.why_unclear: The operative clinical criteria live in a separate published Practice Standard that was not supplied with this Authority; nothing may be invented to fill them.

open_questions.topic: No dose, strength, frequency or duration printed for the listed medicines
open_questions.observed: Clause 2 lists oral forms only: celecoxib, etoricoxib, indometacin, ketoprofen, meloxicam, naproxen immediate-release, naproxen modified-release, piroxicam, diclofenac. No dose, strength, frequency, max_dose or quantity_to_supply values are printed anywhere in the 4-page instrument (the only numeric supply limit is 'longer than 12 weeks' in clause 3(d)).
open_questions.why_unclear: Dosing detail is deferred to the external Practice Standard; treatment fields are left empty rather than inferred.

open_questions.topic: Approved pharmacist training options table reads imperfectly
open_questions.observed: On page 3 the training-options table extracts as interleaved fragments: 'The Queensland James Cook University's / University of Extended community / Prescribing Technology's Safe OR practice pharmacists / training / prescribing and quality course (subject PC6300 / use of medicines course only). AND / Clinical / James Cook University's Extended community practice / practice / training / pharmacists course (subjects PC6100 and PC6200 only).'
open_questions.why_unclear: Two-column table layout is misaligned in text extraction; the exact wording and structure of the training options cannot be transcribed with confidence.

open_questions.topic: No urgent or emergency referral destinations printed
open_questions.observed: The instrument contains no urgent or emergency referral list; the only referral wording is the clause 3(e) cross-reference to the Practice Standard.
open_questions.why_unclear: Document is silent; empty urgent/emergency arrays reflect the source rather than an extraction gap.

open_questions.topic: Commencement date not printed as a calendar date
open_questions.observed: Clause 6: 'This authority commences on publication.' Clause 7: 'This authority is cancelled on 1 March 2027, unless earlier cancelled.' The instrument is dated 25 February 2026.
open_questions.why_unclear: Effective date depends on the publication date, which is not stated in the document.

open_questions.observed: No notifiable-condition, Australian Immunisation Register or mandatory adverse-event reporting requirement is printed. 'notifiable.required = true' reflects only the consent-based sharing of the consultation record with the patient's usual treating medical practitioner (clause 3(j), page 3).
open_questions.why_unclear: Document is silent on notifiable conditions; recorded so the flag is not misread.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Load the NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Mild, Acute Musculoskeletal Pain (approved by the Chief Health Officer) and transcribe its duration-of-management quantities, age/other-factor supply limitations and referral circumstances before go-live.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Clause 3(b) and 3(e) make supply conditional on content that is not printed in this instrument; the rules engine cannot evaluate INC-4/EXC-5/EXC-8/RF-1 without it.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the 12-week absolute supply cap (clause 3(d)) is implemented as a hard check alongside the Practice Standard quantity limits, including the smallest-manufacturer-pack exception in clause 3(c).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Seeded supply-limit rule that a pharmacist must confirm before go-live; the exception interacts with the cap.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Verify the approved-pharmacist training options (two-column table on page 3, including James Cook University subjects PC6300 / PC6100 / PC6200 and the Queensland University of Technology Safe prescribing and quality use of medicines course) directly against the PDF.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Table extracts as garbled interleaved text; training completion is a precondition of the authority.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm local policy for recording and storing the clinical record for a minimum of seven (7) years (clause 3(i)) and for displaying the pharmacist's name at or near the consultation room (clause 3(h)).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Operational requirements left to the pharmacy's implementation; must be confirmed before go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm handling of the publication/commencement date and the 1 March 2027 cancellation date in the prescribing module.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Commencement is 'on publication' with no calendar date printed; expiry must gate the protocol's availability.
